idea: Multi‑hop question answering often relies on reasoning over a chain of facts in a knowledge graph, yet current language‑model training typically uses isolated head‑relation‑tail triples, depriving the model of the surrounding context that supports multi‑step inference. We propose to enrich each target triple (or path) with additional triples drawn from the same source passage, forming a local context subgraph that is presented together with the primary supervision signal. The model will be fine‑tuned under two regimes: one using only the target triple/path and another that also incorporates the supporting context. To improve the reliability of the base facts, we will introduce an adaptive repair loop that detects one‑hop failures, generates corrective examples, and iteratively refines the model. After this cleaning stage, we will apply reinforcement‑learning‑based optimization on lower‑hop QA instances and evaluate transfer to deeper multi‑hop queries.
